title: Edit a reading-room paragraph for precision
instructions: A student drafted this paragraph: ‘After volunteers opened a weekend reading room in an unused shop unit, the project made things better for local pupils. At first, the room had a bad system for returned books, so helpers did a new shelf arrangement. They also got advice from pupils about opening hours. The change was amazing, and everyone always found every book immediately.’ Use only these verified notes when editing: returned books were sometimes left unsorted until the next session; volunteers introduced labelled return trays and a reshelving rota; pupil feedback showed that older students wanted Sunday afternoon hours; by the third weekend, most returns were reshelved on the day they arrived; 18 pupils attended the added Sunday session. Answer all six questions before viewing feedback.

parts.prompt: Which THREE expressions most clearly require precision because they are vague or stronger than the verified notes?

options.text: made things better
in an unused shop unit
had a bad system
about opening hours
amazing, and everyone always found every book immediately

choice_rationales.A: The phrase does not identify what changed or how pupils benefited.
choice_rationales.B: This is a concrete, neutral description of the location.
choice_rationales.C: The judgement ‘bad’ hides the observable problem with unsorted returns.
choice_rationales.D: This accurately names the subject on which feedback was collected.
choice_rationales.E: ‘Amazing’, ‘everyone’, ‘always’ and ‘every’ make sweeping claims that the notes do not establish.

parts.hint: Select wording that either conceals the observable meaning or exceeds the evidence.
parts.correct_explanation: Precise editing targets vague labels and unsupported absolutes while retaining concrete, accurate details.

parts.prompt: Which replacement most precisely revises ‘helpers did a new shelf arrangement’ using the verified notes?

options.text: The helpers executed a magnificent organisational transformation.
The volunteers introduced labelled return trays and a reshelving rota.
The helpers did something new with the shelves.
The volunteers completely solved the library forever.

choice_rationales.A: The inflated register praises the change without identifying it clearly.
choice_rationales.B: The verb and nouns name the two recorded actions accurately and naturally.
choice_rationales.C: The revision preserves the vague verb and object.
choice_rationales.D: The absolute claim is wider and stronger than the project notes support.

parts.hint: Choose the sentence that lets a reader picture the recorded action without adding praise or permanence.
parts.correct_explanation: ‘Introduced’ combines naturally with the two exact measures recorded in the notes.

parts.prompt: Which revision of ‘got advice from pupils about opening hours’ has the most accurate meaning, collocation and register?

options.text: harvested pupil opinions concerning temporal accessibility
got some nice ideas from the pupils
collected pupil feedback on opening hours
proved that all pupils demanded longer opening hours

choice_rationales.A: The words are inflated, and ‘harvested opinions’ is an unnatural partnership here.
choice_rationales.C: ‘Collected feedback’ is a natural partnership and states the evidence neutrally.
choice_rationales.D: The notes concern older students and Sunday afternoons, not every pupil or all opening hours.

parts.hint: Test the whole phrase for natural partnership and compare its strength with the notes.
parts.correct_explanation: The revision uses an accurate collocation and a clear school-essay register without overstating the finding.

parts.prompt: Which sentence uses repetition to maintain a clear reference chain rather than forcing an unnecessary synonym?

options.text: Returned books went into labelled trays, and most returns were reshelved on the day they arrived.
Returned books went into labelled trays, and most literary commodities were reshelved promptly.
Returned books went into labelled trays, and most things were dealt with.
Returned books went into labelled trays, and the excellent items enjoyed immediate shelf restoration.

choice_rationales.A: ‘Returns’ repeats the central term in a shorter form and keeps the meaning stable.
choice_rationales.B: ‘Literary commodities’ changes the register and makes the reference less natural.
choice_rationales.C: ‘Things’ weakens the reference and removes the recorded result.
choice_rationales.D: The wording personifies books, adds praise and turns a bounded result into immediacy.

parts.hint: A repeated key term can be useful when alternatives would blur its referent.
parts.correct_explanation: Controlled repetition supports cohesion; synonym variety is not valuable when it distorts a central term.

parts.prompt: Which result sentence stays within the verified evidence?

options.text: The changes transformed literacy throughout the entire neighbourhood.
By the third weekend, most returns were reshelved on the day they arrived, and 18 pupils attended the added Sunday session.
Every pupil immediately found every book and became a regular reader.
The project was extremely good and completely successful.

choice_rationales.A: The notes do not measure neighbourhood literacy or establish a transformation.
choice_rationales.B: Both observations reproduce the scope, timing and quantities in the notes without claiming more.
choice_rationales.C: The universal behaviour and later reading habit were not observed.
choice_rationales.D: The evaluation is vague and absolute instead of presenting the available results.

parts.hint: Prefer bounded observations to broad claims about success or long-term impact.
parts.correct_explanation: Exact times, quantities and limits are precise only when they come from the evidence.

parts.prompt: Which revised paragraph uses precise vocabulary most effectively throughout?

options.text: The reading room made things better. Its bad returns system was fixed, and pupils gave nice ideas. The result was amazing.
The initiative effectuated a comprehensive transformation by harvesting stakeholder insights and optimising literary-item logistics.

The volunteers opened a weekend reading room in an unused shop unit, but returned books were sometimes left unsorted until the next session. They introduced labelled return trays and a reshelving rota, and they collected pupil feedback on opening hours. After older students requested Sunday afternoon access, the team added a session that 18 pupils attended. By the third weekend, most returns were reshelved on the day they arrived.
The volunteers introduced three trays and therefore raised every pupil’s reading ability, eliminated all delays and permanently improved the neighbourhood.

choice_rationales.A: The paragraph relies on vague labels and praise instead of observable actions and results.
choice_rationales.B: Inflated wording obscures simple actions and includes awkward word partnerships.
choice_rationales.C: The nouns and verbs are specific, the register is natural, repetition is controlled and every claim remains within the notes.
choice_rationales.D: It invents a tray count and makes unsupported causal, universal and permanent claims.

parts.hint: Choose the paragraph in which precise language makes the evidence clearer without exaggeration or thesaurus display.
parts.correct_explanation: Effective vocabulary editing aligns exact wording with the writer's meaning, the natural phrase, the intended register and the evidence available.
